title: A.T.O.M Workspace, Information Architecture & Product UX Audit
purpose: Freeze the product shell and observable behavior before a future Concept 7G implementation.
scope: Documentation-only audit. No RF, optimizer, domain, persistence, IndexedDB, API, or UI behavior changes are part of Concept 7F.

responsiveBreakpoints.behavior: Full header context, left rail, drawer, and map toolbar. 1440px and 1280px observations were usable.
Header hides brand subtitle, plan summary, save state, and result summary as width decreases.
Result summary is hidden; drawer/rail remain side-by-side. 1024px observation showed map toolbar and subnav crowding.
Map fills the viewport, workflow rail becomes a bottom rail, and the drawer becomes a bottom sheet. The toolbar remains dense; at 640px the layer menu extended roughly 114px beyond the viewport.
Some map controls wrap and labels collapse, but this is a best-effort inspection layout rather than a full planning workflow.

observedViewports.finding: Map remains dominant; header, rail, drawer, toolbar, legend, and Setup/Scenario content are readable.
Still usable for the core map workflow; drawer and toolbar consume a meaningful but acceptable share of width.
Header is intentionally reduced, but toolbar controls clip or crowd the right edge; result tabs wrap; advanced drawers feel overloaded.
Bottom-sheet map shell is visible; layer menu overflow and toolbar density make full planning/editing unreliable.

bundleSnapshot.warning: Vite warns that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB after minification.
bundleSnapshot.interpretation: Worth measuring and eventually code-splitting by product boundary; not a reason for an emergency optimization-only phase.

positiveEvidence: Visible focus styles exist for common controls.
Many status, alert, listbox, option, tab, table, and graphic roles are present.
Map toolbar buttons expose aria-labels and narrow controls maintain a 44px minimum target in CSS.
risks: ToolDrawer uses a native dialog element with aria-modal=false but is a modeless application drawer; focus containment and return-to-trigger behavior were not evident.
Map markers and rich map layers are visually informative but do not provide a complete keyboard-equivalent inspection path.
Rail status badges and some icon-first controls need text/state context beyond color or a symbol; labels exist in several places but consistency should be verified.
The full application has a large focusable surface and no client route state, making deep-linking and restoration of context difficult for keyboard and assistive-technology users.

keyEvidence: App.jsx renders every major panel in one shell and imports all research/reference panels eagerly.
WorkspaceChrome owns the global header, rail, drawer, map toolbar, legend, and project menu.
workspaceTools.js defines four stages and thirteen tools without route-backed navigation.
ScenarioPanel and ProjectMenu both expose Version actions.
DataPanel combines dataset, model assumptions, field validation, and calibration.
Propagation and RF Diagnostics combine everyday controls with specialized reference workflows.

validationIntent: JSON parsing for every Concept 7F JSON artifact
